create.title: Nonsquare reciprocal divisor-strip incidence and exact-center closure
create.statement_tex: Let J=sqrt X, 1<=L<=H<=J^(1/2), and retain the accepted complete collar-extracted top-M2 coefficient. For primitive odd coprime nonsquare rays a<b<4a, put m=(a+b)/2, q=(b-a)/2, u=q/(m+sqrt(m^2-q^2)), and Lambda=Xqu. Then (sqrt(b)-sqrt(a))^2/2=qu and the literal reciprocal interval is Ju/(1-u)<k<2Ju/(1+u). On a dyadic block a asymp A, b-a asymp D, k asymp K, G_(a,b) asymp G, let P be the number of actual residual rays and M_(a,b)(K) the literal reciprocal-mode count. For every 1<=R<=N_(a,b)<<G, the metric incidence satisfies I_ns<<_(epsilon,c)X^epsilon sum_(a,b) min(M_(a,b)(K),1+K/R)<<X^epsilon P(1+K/R). Since K asymp JD/A, R<=G asymp L/A, and L<=J^(1/2), this is <<X^epsilon ADK/R. The complete coefficient scale is V<<X^epsilon A sqrt(G)/sqrt(JD); after the Abel weight and standalone Abel-1 term, the positive block capacity is <<X^epsilon A sqrt(G)sqrt(J)D^(3/2), so all blocks AJD^3<<L^3 are target-sized after dyadic summation. If ab=d r^2 with d>1 squarefree, rational ratios of m-r sqrt(d) force the same primitive ray. Hence at fixed X at most one primitive nonsquare ray is exactly resonant, and all its divisor modes contribute O_epsilon(LX^epsilon) absolutely. Two distinct metric incidences further imply R<<A^5D^2K^7, improved to R<<AD^2K^3 in one squarefree field, but these thresholds are outside the active metric range. No signed estimate is claimed on the remaining strict-metric blocks AJD^3>>L^3.

create.title: Random-density obstruction to algebraic classification of all nonsquare metric resonances
create.statement_tex: Fix a uniformly populated geometric inner cone of primitive nonsquare rays and reciprocal integers that stays strictly inside the literal k interval while X ranges over [Y,2Y]. For each dyadic metric width 1/R, elementary periodic averaging gives mean incidence (2c/R)#T plus an endpoint error smaller in the active range. Exact equalities have measure zero, so the same baseline may be strictly metric. On a fixed-ratio B-block with asymp B^2 primitive geometric rays and asymp sqrt(Y) reciprocal modes per ray, some real X has >>B^2 sqrt(Y)/R metric incidences; near-square rays b=a+2 give the analogous >>sqrt(Y)/R baseline. Mapping this geometric statement to the literal complete lift requires a populated actual subblock with N_(a,b)>=R and does not provide an actual coefficient lower bound. It rigorously shows that the factor-R divisor-strip estimate is sharp at ordinary density and that a future inverse theorem may classify only excess over density 1/R. The density part itself still requires a signed complete-coefficient estimate; coefficient-blind positive summation leaves capacity A sqrt(G)sqrt(J)D^(3/2).
create.next_action: Do not launch another coefficient-blind inverse classification. Estimate the signed density component and centered discrepancy together using the literal primitive-ray coefficient.

reject.reason: Averaging the prescribed real X produces the ordinary 1/R population even after exact equalities and primitive square rays are removed, and the incidences may span many squarefree fields.
The factor-R divisor-strip saving exactly cancels the Abel weight R and leaves positive capacity A sqrt(G)sqrt(J)D^(3/2), which is too large on AJD^3>>L^3.
The metric strip contains O(K/R) distinct nearby integers p=ell k. Exact centers form only one absolutely safe subcase.
The norm thresholds R<<A^5D^2K^7 and R<<AD^2K^3 lie far beyond R<=L/A, and multiplication by arbitrary real X creates ordinary modulo-one clustering.
Reversing p=ell k merely lists the same integer-product fibers and supplies no independent oscillation or curvature.
